veranderings.rede: The Afrikaans idiom is 'jou keel trek toe'; 'voel toe' is unidiomatic.

veranderings.voor: swaar en moeg en wil jy
veranderings.na: swaar en moeg, en wil jy
veranderings.rede: AWS comma before 'en' joining two clauses with their own subject and verb (jou lyf voel / wil jy), as elsewhere in the lesson.

veranderings.blok: Voel vir hom en wil help
veranderings.rede: 'nie noodwendig' is the natural Afrikaans for 'does not necessarily mean'; 'nie vanself' reads oddly here.

veranderings.blok: Voel vir hom en wil help
veranderings.na: Jy wys dit gewoonlik met wat jy doen
veranderings.rede: Sitting down next to someone is not done with the hands, so the image does not fit its own example; 'gewoonlik' is kept.

veranderings.voor: Sê dit vir 'n grootmens wat jy vertrou as jou maat lank swaarkry of as hy in gevaar is.
veranderings.na: As jou maat lank swaarkry of as hy in gevaar is, sê dit vir 'n grootmens wat jy vertrou.
veranderings.rede: 'vertrou as' can be misread as 'trust as'; putting the condition first reads clearly and lets the next sentence follow on 'grootmens'.
'vra' has no object here, so it is unclear what is asked; 'gaan na die volgende een' keeps the meaning of turning to the next adult.

veranderings.na: Om te verstaan en saam te voel deur jou
veranderings.rede: A definition starting with bare verbs reads as a fragment; the 'Om te' form matches the deernis entry.
A comma after the embedded relative clause keeps 'swaarkry te voel' from running together for a young reader.

vlae.teks: Hy dra dit ook nie alleen nie.
vlae.rede: 'dit' has no clear antecedent (the burden is never named), and as a plain statement it says the friend does not carry it alone rather than that he need not; 'Hy hoef dit ook nie alleen te dra nie' may be meant, but that shifts the meaning, so a writer should decide.
